articles.title: Heads up, Fallout 4 and Skyrim players: New updates are incoming, so it's time to tend to your mods
articles.subtitle: The new patch, featuring "Creations improvements," is set to roll out on August 18.
articles.author: PC Gamer
articles.content:
Bethesda Game Studios is warning owners of Fallout 4 to either log into a save or manually save their mod load order, because a new patch "focusing on general Creations improvements" is incoming.

Bethesda's got a bit of interesting history when it comes to Fallout 4 patches. 2024's "next gen" update didn't really improve anything but did manage to break quite a lot, and the best solution to come out of that whole thing was simply to roll it all back with a "Downgrader Tool." A year after that, Bethesda did it again, although on a somewhat smaller scale, except that ended up causing a surprise new round of headaches, resulting in much wailing and gnashing of teeth, and of course another update.

All of which is to say that if you're a Fallout 4 fan, you should probably pay heed to Bethesda's latest heads-up.

"As a precaution, prior to these updates we encourage players to log into your game save if you haven't done so in a while or manually save your load order," the studio wrote (via Polygon ). "Once your load order is saved, you'll be able to re-download your entire Creations list at once when the update is live."

On Tuesday, August 18th, a patch will be coming to Fallout 4 focusing on general Creations improvements.As a precaution, prior to these updates we encourage players to log into your game save if you haven’t done so in a while or manually save your load order. The response to the post is an interesting mix of gratitude that an 11-year-old game is still being actively supported, concern about the damage that ongoing support might cause, and bemusement/outrage that Bethesda is dicking around with Fallout 4 instead of working on Elder Scrolls 6. My guess is that the studio is capable of doing both, but sometimes you just have to get this stuff off your chest.

In any event, this will hopefully not cause any major headaches, but it's still good advice. And speaking of The Elder Scrolls, Bethesda also said that it's working on a new Skyrim update, details of which will be revealed later. articles.title: Apple’s AI announcements: One big question, and 11 key features
articles.subtitle: Almost two years after Apple first showed off a video promoting the new Siri and lots of exciting new Apple Intelligence features, that future has finally arrived – at least in first beta form. The company had a lot of ground to make up.
articles.author: 9to5Mac Apple Intelligence
articles.content:
Almost two years after Apple first showed off a video promoting the new Siri and lots of exciting new Apple Intelligence features, that future has finally arrived – at least in first beta form.

The company had a lot of ground to make up. Obviously, the test will be how well the new features work in real life usage, but let’s start with what seemed to me to be the most important things the company announced …

The big iPhone support question

For me, one of the biggest questions to arise from the keynote was exactly what features will require the iPhone 17 Pro and up?

Apple had three things to say about iPhone support. The first says that any phone capable of running iOS 26 can be upgraded to iOS 27. That means all the way back to the iPhone 11.

The second is that the new AI features only extend back to the iPhone 15 Pro:

Apple Intelligence and Siri AI in iOS 27, iPadOS 27, macOS 27, watchOS 27, and visionOS 27 are available on iPhone 16 models or later, iPhone 15 Pro, iPhone 15 Pro Max.

The third says that some features are limited to just the latest and greatest models.

Apple’s most powerful on-device model and the features it enables, like expressive voices and more advanced dictation, are available on iPhone Air, iPhone 17 Pro, iPhone 17 Pro Max.

The word ‘like’ is doing a lot of heavy lifting there: it means we don’t yet know what other features will fall into this category. Additionally, it’s not yet 100% clear whether phones that can’t perform these actions on-device will still get access to the same features, just relying on cloud connectivity.

This latter question is especially important when it comes to advanced dictation. However smart the new Siri may be, it first needs to understand what we are saying. The existing Siri speech-to-text capabilities fall way short of what is available from third-parties.

The overall model seems well-considered

Apple’s general approach here is to make Siri’s new capabilities transparently available system-wide. In other words, we can ask our iPhone to do something and the new Siri will step in to perform the task.

However, there are times when it’s useful to revisit an earlier chatbot session, and Apple allows us to do this through the Siri app. That seems to me the best of both worlds. We don’t need to open Siri to do anything requiring the new Apple Intelligence features, but we can access past sessions when required.

Agentic AI is key

The ability to ask our iPhone to carry out a task and have it be able to access not only the personal information we have stored on our phone, but also interact with apps, is absolutely key to truly useful AI.

Again, we will need to see how well this really works, but Apple does seem to be ticking all of the boxes in terms of the capabilities I was looking for.

articles.title: Fan-Favorite Star Trek FPS Had To Change Its Plot After 9/11: ‘We Actually Had A Shuttle Fly Into a Building’
articles.subtitle: 9/11 GTA 3 Star Trek Star Trek: Elite Force 2 is a very fun first-person shooter that arrived on PC in June 2002. While it might have been a commercial flop at the time, it has gone on to become a fan-favorite Star Trek game featuring a nice mix of puzzles,...
articles.author: Kotaku
articles.content:
9/11 GTA 3 Star Trek

Star Trek: Elite Force 2 is a very fun first-person shooter that arrived on PC in June 2002. While it might have been a commercial flop at the time, it has gone on to become a fan-favorite Star Trek game featuring a nice mix of puzzles, action, and dialogue. But the game would have been a whole lot different if the terrorist attacks against the United States hadn’t happened on September 11, 2001.

In a new interview with FRVR, Star Trek: Elite Force 2 lead scripter and level designer Benson Russell explained that during the development of the game, the story and opening of the game had to change in a big way due to the attacks on 9/11.

“I remember, we were making Elite Force 2, and 9/11 happened at that time,” Russell told FRVR. “One of the original scenes was, when you were at Starfleet Academy, it was supposed to get an attack, and we actually had a shuttle fly into a building and stuff like that.”

As you might expect, Elite Force 2 arriving less than a year after September 11 meant that all of that content had to be cut or reworked entirely. “Well, that was a no-no for understandable reasons, of course,” said Russell.

Despite the cuts and changes, Elite Force 2 became a popular Star Trek game that people still talk about fondly to this day. And they should, because it’s a great FPS powered by id Tech 3 that any fan of that era of Star Trek should play, if only because you get some wonderful, low-poly Picard moments. And yes, he’s voiced by Patrick Stewart.

Famously, Rockstar Games found itself in a similar situation around this time. Its 2001 game, Grand Theft Auto 3, was set in a contemporary New York City-like open world, and so the studio had to make numerous changes, including making the police cars look less like actual NYPD vehicles as planned and more generic.

Interestingly, 9/11 also forced Rockstar to change the cover of GTA 3 before launch in the United States. ( The European release used the cover art originally planned. ) That cover became so iconic and popular that it ended up establishing the style that all GTA covers would follow to this day. Even the upcoming GTA 6 cover follows that same grid-based look created back in 2001 in response to 9/11.
